Assign regulatory standards

Source: R/standards.R
assign_standards.Rd

Assigns regulatory, screening, permit, background, or project-specific standards to environmental chemistry results.

assign_standards(df, standards = standards_tbl)

Arguments

df

Environmental chemistry data as an env_schema object.

standards

Standards table or standards_schema object. Defaults to standards_tbl.

Value

An enriched env_schema containing matched standard metadata, including standard values, units, categories, and related fields from the standards schema.

Schema attributes from df are preserved.

Details

Standards are matched using the analyte name stored in .analyte. Matching is performed through [as_standards_schema()] and [.match_standards()], which attach the highest-priority applicable standard to each observation.

If multiple standards match a result, the standard with the lowest .priority value is retained.

Following assignment, standard values are converted to the analytical units present in .analysis_unit so that exceedance comparisons can be performed directly.

When multiple standards apply to a result, the standard with the lowest .priority value is assigned.

Recommended priority ranges are:

  • 1-9 = Site- or project-specific objectives

  • 10-19 = Permit limits and compliance criteria

  • 20-49 = Regulatory standards

  • 50-99 = Screening levels and guidance values

  • 100+ = Background or informational values

See also

[`as_standards_schema`()], [standards_tbl]
